lines.en: It’s been a week since I’ve heard anything from Karin.
Which is fair, of course.
I mean, I did force myself on top of her in a private room and all. Even if it wasn’t really me doing the forcing.
But considering that I haven’t received so much as a follow-up from anyone she knows makes me think she didn’t tell anyone. And of course, that makes me question why.
Perhaps it’s shock or embarrassment or shame or any of the reasons that made Molly keep things to herself after my run-in with her, but this is different than that.
For this, I was there — and forced to bear witness to the horrible things I was doing as I struggled to regain control of my body and my tongue.
I guess it was deserved in a way, though. I’ve grown so complacent in the doing of my misdeeds that I’m all but desensitized to the vast majority of them at this point.
And the last time something like this happened, everything went dark in a much more literal sense. This time, I couldn’t even find a corner in the shadows of my mind to crawl to for safety.
But maybe it was the fact that I was still somewhat there this time that let me pull away before anything terrible happened.
Well, more terrible. I can’t imagine being tackled by an adult male will do many favors for Karin’s androphobia.
But one thing’s for sure, and it’s that I need to apologize. Sooner rather than later.
Everything happened so fast that night in the karaoke booth that it was like the two of us just vanished.
And while I’ve somehow managed to survive that once again, maybe Karin didn’t.
Maybe she actually did vanish. And maybe the reason that I haven’t heard from her is that she’s decided to sever ties with me completely.
That’d make her the smartest out of everyone.
But it would do nothing for me.
So I tap on her name in my phone and wait for her to answer.
And of course she doesn’t because that would have made things too easy.
So, if I’m going to apologize to her, I’m going to have to do it the old fashioned way — by scouring town in the places she visits most for a chance to see her.
Waiting behind a tree or under the cover of darkness before jumping out and confronting her with a problem she’s afraid to confront on her own.
She’ll likely be too shocked to run, that poor fainting goat of a girl.
But if paralyzing her legs is what I must do to make me feel like I’m a good person, by God will I do it.
I’m a better boy now.
I have so much to show the world.
Suddenly, the bell rings.
Suddenly, I move to the front door.
Suddenly, I open it.
And suddenly, she is here.
Because, once again, I never have to work for anything.
It’s amazing what you can have delivered nowadays.
: Karin...
: I got your call.
: That was like five minutes ago. Did you fly here?
: No. I’ve been in front of your house for like ten minutes trying to think of what I want to say.
: Why should you have to say anything? You didn’t do anything wrong.
: I know that. You did. But what I can’t figure out is why.
: You’ve been nothing but nice to me since we met. And apart from my dad, you were the only man I ever kind of...opened up to.
: Was all of that just a lie?
: Sometimes, lying is necessary to create the kind of future you want.
: And what kind of future is it that you want? How does leading me on make that achievable for you?
: I’ve never lied to you, Karin.
: You’re lying again right now, Sensei.
: I might be naive, but I’m not an idiot. I’m one of the smartest girls in my grade. And even if I’m inexperienced with men, I can still tell when somebody is leading me on.
: You think I’m leading you on?
: Are you not? Because everything you said when you had me pinned down seemed like it was tailor-made to make me bend to your will.
: I trusted you...How could you do that to me?
: I didn’t want to, Karin.
: You didn’t want to? Am I just supposed to believe that?
: Listen...do you want to come inside and-
: No. No way. I am not coming inside your house. Not after what you did to me. If we’re going to talk, we can do it out here.

Karin takes a step back and nearly knocks over the neighbor’s bike- and I have to prevent myself from reflexively reaching forward to stop it from falling because I know that doing that will just scare her now.
That’s just an obstacle I’m always going to have to deal with from now on, I guess.
And yes, it’s my fault. Yes, the burden of the reflex itself will weigh heavier on her than it does on me. But it’s one more added inconvenience to a life already full of them.
I don’t have room for many more.
: That...is fair. I’m sorry for suggesting it.
: It’s...fine. I just...
: I...need to know just what was real and what was fake. Because...you were important to me. In a way that other people never were...
: Do you understand what I'm saying?...
: Do you like me, Karin?
: I mean...I’m in high school. You’re way older than me and...it’s hard to tell if what I felt for you was just...admiration or...you know...other stuff, but...
: But now...
: I’m kind of just...afraid of you.
: I used to smile every time Kirin or somebody else brought you up. Now, I just want to cry.
: And so...it might be pointless for me to come here and try to find closure or...even an answer to any of my questions. Especially since you’re not even coming to school anymore.

: But I felt like I had to...because I don’t want to feel those depressing feelings anymore. I have a younger sister I need to set a good example for. And I can’t do that if my head won’t stop spinning.
: So you’re confronting the same man who pinned you down head-on? Isn’t that a little too...daring?
: Is that a threat? Because I’m more than willing to walk away now. I just thought things might not come to that because of the way they left off.
: When you pulled yourself off of me, you looked different. You looked regretful. Was that a lie too? Do you only regret it because I kept saying no?
: What was that, Sensei? All of it. Why? Why would you do that?
: I won’t ask you to come inside again, but would you like to maybe...go for a walk or something? So I can try to explain.
: A walk where? Because I’d like to stay in public for now.

: Just down the road. We probably don’t have to worry about Ami leaving her room right now, but I’d still feel a little more comfortable knowing she can’t pop out and listen to this whenever she wants.
: Yeah...I’d want to keep this a secret from her if I were you as well.
: Come on...let’s go.
Karin takes off down the same path I used to take to school every morning.
And while I am no stranger to descending this seemingly never-ending flight of stone steps, it feels different this time. It feels harder.
And here I thought hanging my head would have the opposite effect.
Not wanting to get too far away from Ami, I point to a nearby bench and the two of us take a seat.
I’m surprised when Karin lets me sit beside her, but I guess she feels a little more secure knowing that there would be onlookers if I were to try something again.
Unfortunately for her, I’m not sure such a thing would stop me. But, then again, I still have no clue what the new voices in my head even want, so maybe they’re just waiting for me to get her alone.
Whatever the case, they’re not bothering me today.
Like I said a week ago, some days are worse than others.
And all we can do is hope things stay that way.
: Before I start saying a whole bunch of things that won’t make any sense to you, I just want you to know that you’re one of the last people I’d ever want to hurt.
: It’s probably hard to believe that right now given what I did last week, but it’s true. You’re one of the few irrefutably kind souls I’ve encountered in this city.
: So much so that I feel like even being near you is a sin. Like some...parasite is going to fall out of my ears and latch onto you and turn you less good or something.
: That’s...kind of gross...
: Yeah...it is. Isn’t it?
: Karin, I’m a miserable man.
: And I’ve been that way forever, I think.
: You already know a little about my memory issues, but something I don’t think you understand yet is what other sorts of...malfunctions I’ve got going on in my head.
: You know how in cartoons, they’ll always use a devil and an angel on someone’s shoulders to symbolize their conscience? Well...for me, there is no angel. And I never even get to see the devil.
: He’s there. I can hear him almost constantly. And he’s taken up residence somewhere inside of me that I’m pretty sure I’d never even be able to reach without the help of a shotgun.
: Sensei, stop.
: I’m not going to do anything, don’t worry. I’m too much of a coward. And this alone is barely enough to call an explanation or...even an excuse.
: I’m just not me sometimes. Like, I can’t control myself. And before I know it, I’m doing something terrible or...just did something terrible.
: But then I switch back to normal and have to deal with the aftermath.
: Doesn’t that sound a little too...um...convenient? As an excuse, I mean.
: Anyone can do bad things to people and then say that something made them do it. And that’s rarely ever true.

: I know that. Which is why I don’t expect you to believe me and am prepared for this to be the last talk we ever have. I’m just trying to explain myself since I think it would be good for you to have closure too.
: It’s been really hard for me ever since Halloween. I lost someone I loved. And it’s affecting me in ways that, while expected, are still pretty fucking unexpected.
: And if that sounds contradictory, it’s because it is.
: I know that it’s nearly impossible to predict how grief or loss will hit a person. But if you told me a year or two ago the state I’d be in now, I’d likely have laughed in your face.
: I’m not emotionally equipped to deal with things like loss. I’m not you. And yeah, I’m older, but that doesn’t mean I’m any more whole...or even someone you should look up to.
: I’m...sorry to hear all of that, Sensei. But I still don’t think any of that explains why you tackled me the way you did.
: I don’t think anything can explain why I tackled you the way I did. So if that’s the sort of closure you’re looking for, I’m not going to be able to help.
: But if you want to know how much was real and how much was fake, I’m going to need more specific questions.
: Specific, huh?...
: Then...let’s start with this.
: Were you...already aware of how I felt about you?
: Yes.
: Did you know Miku was going to leave us alone?
: She mentioned something about it earlier. But there was a lot more on my mind when we made it to the karaoke booth.
: What was on your mind?
: Something completely unrelated to both of you.
: Are you attracted to me?
: Yes.
: Do you know how old I am?
: And that doesn’t change anything about the way you feel?
: I really wish it did.
: Have you ever thought about hurting me before?
: Not intentionally.
: Why think that way at all?
: Because I think that way about everyone. I can’t help it.
: If I didn’t try to stop you...what would you have done?
: Would you have followed through?...
: Or would the outcome have been the same?
: I really have no clue...
: Have you been grooming me this entire time?
: Karin...
: Have you been faking it all along? All those phone calls...all those conversations...was all of that just to make me let you in?
: It’s a lot more complicated than that...
: Do you love me, Sensei?
: No.
: Thanks for clearing all of that up.
: I know how it sounds...but I didn’t want to do that, Karin. I seriously couldn’t help it. I’d never do anything like that to you on purpose.
: No...you’d just string me along until you know that I trust you...
: You’d pepper me with compliments...and flirt with me despite knowing how I felt...while continuing to call me and hang out with me, but never intending to actually take things anywhere...
: I’ve just been a toy for you, haven’t I?
: No...you’re so much more than that.
: You know...
: It feels weird to say this...but I’d be way more inclined to forgive you right now if you told me you just got caught up in the moment back then.
: If what you wanted when you tackled me was real...and you were just misreading the moment or...misunderstanding my experience with stuff like that...
: That would have been so much better than finding out none of it meant anything.
: Just because I don’t love you doesn’t mean I can never-
: Sensei...I’m sorry, but you’ll never be able to love anyone like this.
: And I don’t know what it was that made your world go dark, but I hope you can figure out how to move past it.
: You’re really pitiful like this. But the worst part is I can’t even feel bad for you since it’s all your fault.
: Karin-
: I won’t tell anyone about what happened since you did come clean...but I do think you should stay away from my sister and me for a while.
: I don’t feel safe when you’re around. And I don’t want you hurting her either.
: I’m gonna go home now...but thanks for talking to me.
: And please...try to figure yourself out.
: You’re nothing like the man I thought you were.
In that moment, I finally find the benefit of hanging my head.
It’s that I don’t have to see her walk away.
As I head back home, I make one more mental note amidst a sea of pre-existing annotations.
All this one says is that her chapter is still open.
And that I was a fool for thinking I could jump to the epilogue.
Karin’s affection has decreased by 10!
It isn’t until nightfall that I’m ready to go back outside.
